newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares firmer in bullish market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares firmer in bullish market.

text.p: Zimbabwe's key industrial index surged 63.50 points to a new all-time high of 10,993.42 on Monday, fuelled by continued high investor appetite for equities, brokers said.
They said investors, discouraged by more-or-less stagnant interest rates on the local market, were drifting back to the bourse which promised better returns on their money.
"The trend is upward at the moment and I expect the demand (for stocks) to continue," one broker said.

Counters to advance on Monday included pharmaceutical group Caps which climbed 200 cents higher to 2,500 while finance house Finhold put on 50 cents to 900 and blue chip conglomerate Delta and cement firm Circem were both up 40 cents to 1,850 and 540 respectively.
Other gains were in food company Natfood which added 20 cents to 520, with cool drink firm Schweppes at 410 and pork processors Colcom at 460 both going up 10 cents.

Minings on the other hand showed little life with most counters there trading unchanged while coal miners Wankie put on 10 cents to 610 and nickel producers Bindura shed 20 cents to 600. The seven-share mining index lost 6.82 points to 863.95.
